purpose: Recommend a generic scalable-publication/search design for GuavaJam and its optional static generator, supported by retained real Riverhog contract/NAV corpus, exact-source storage/query experiments and actual browser delivery experiments. Reference-only scripts and an aggregate-guard experiment patch are supplied; production runtime remains at the inspected base.
producer: ChatGPT, with parallel corpus, search-architecture and transport/Proffer research agents
first_step: Read the owning issue, .reference/design.json and .reference/reproduction.json; compare current main against the pinned base. Run .reference/verify.py and the pinned Proffer checker, then independently reproduce selected storage/query/browser evidence in a separate scratch workspace. Agree scope-specific latency/resource budgets; accept/adapt/defer/reject each proposed generic capability and record consumer disposition in the owning issue against the immutable handoff commit. Evaluate the aggregate-guard patch and prototypes independently; implement selected changes in an integration worktree rather than merging the reference payload.

limitations: Reference-only branch adds .reference artifacts to the pinned base. No runtime integration, main change, merge, deployment or Riverhog migration is included.

Actual source text and production-NAV extraction are real. History, edition work facts/revisions/dates/citation URLs and Example version values are modeled; source byte hashes are of actual serialized fixture GFM, not claims of published releases.

Literal paragraph adapter retains text but does not qualify final tables/lists/links/heading layout or authored manuscript. Arbitrary overlapping source passages cannot be concatenated to reconstruct document text; general storage must capture ordered source blocks.

The proposed bounded production builder is not implemented by the offline storage experiment. Full signed-source validation/rendering/inventories/cache/atomic update are unqualified at this corpus size.

One- and five-edition DBs are measured; 50 edition sensitivity counts text payload only. Full query/source/production-worker matrix is current-edition only; five-edition browser transport covers broad/selective/negative first-page queries.

Browser evidence is Chromium 158 / Playwright 1.64.1 / pinned SQLite WASM 3.54.1-build1 with Node 24.22.3. Repository Node 24.10.0 and bundled Playwright Chromium were not exercised. No Firefox/WebKit/mobile/user DOM journeys or cross-device p95 guarantee.

Controlled HTTP delays 40 ms per response and paces each at nominal 10 Mbit/s; it is not a shared-bandwidth or WAN/mobile simulator. Shared-host contention is visible; original and isolated repeat are retained.
WASM heap, LRU cache byte peaks and transfer bytes are different measures. Total browser/process peak, transient decodes and query temporary allocations are not comprehensively bounded or measured.

Compressed physical chunks use a mechanically adapted third-party VFS scaffold. Length checks exist, but browser hash verification, cancellation, concurrency/recovery/corruption, generation consistency and larger-history maintenance gates remain.
Large-body evidence changes excerpt selection intentionally while retaining primary membership/rank/source/citation. Evidence-window integration and display behavior require review.

Supplemental earlier native-heading receipts have different corpus hashes and are explicitly separated. Historical sub-inventories contain paths to omitted large intermediates or narrative files embedded in guides; the final inventory governs the supplied payload.

The publication-time reproduce.py wrapper was dry-run checked only; the frozen underlying scripts produced the retained measurements. Reproduction commands may require separately installed pinned dependencies and substantial scratch disk/time.
Proffer schema validation and publication identity verification are not consumer acceptance. Consumer disposition belongs in the issue after independent evaluation.
